category: Physics interfaces VI: fluid flow & acoustics features
description: CFD, Microfluidics, Porous Media Flow, Pipe Flow, Mixer and Acoustics Module interfaces and boundary conditions not covered earlier: the turbulence models (k-omega, SST, Spalart-Allmaras, low-Re k-epsilon, LES), Creeping Flow, phase-field and moving-mesh two-phase flow, Level Set/Phase Field interfaces, Nonisothermal Flow, Brinkman, Free and Porous Media Flow, Pipe Flow, High Mach Number Flow, rotating machinery, thin-film flow, multiphase mixture models, shallow water, plus the common flow boundary nodes (symmetry, open boundary, periodic flow, pressure point constraint, fan/screen, boundary stress, wall treatment, inlet types); and the remaining acoustics interfaces (linearized Navier-Stokes/Euler, ray acoustics, poroelastic waves, BEM, time-explicit, convected wave equation, pipe acoustics, acoustic-structure interaction) with their boundary conditions (impedance, port, background pressure field, sound hard/soft, normal acceleration, radiation conditions, point sources, perforated plates, narrow region, poroacoustics, exterior field calculation, periodic).

tools.name: Turbulent Flow, k-omega (spf)
tools.description: RANS single-phase flow interface using the Wilcox k-omega model, which resolves the near-wall region better than k-epsilon (low-Re option, no wall functions needed when the mesh resolves y+ ~ 1) and handles adverse pressure gradients and separation more reliably, at the cost of sensitivity to free-stream omega. Choose it for internal flows with strong curvature, rotating flows and boundary-layer-dominated problems; SST combines its near-wall behaviour with k-epsilon in the free stream.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Turbulent Flow > Turbulent Flow, k-omega (spf); API: physics().create("spf", "TurbulentFlowkomega", "geom1")

parameters.name: Wall treatment
parameters.description: Wall functions | Low Re (Automatic in 6.x switches based on the local mesh).

parameters.name: Turbulence model parameters
parameters.description: Model constants, turbulent Prandtl/Schmidt numbers.

parameters.name: Inlet turbulence
parameters.description: Specify turbulent intensity and length scale or k and omega at inlets.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. Low-Re treatment needs boundary-layer meshes and a Wall Distance Initialization study step (added automatically). Other RANS models in the same menu: k-epsilon (already catalogued), Realizable k-epsilon, Low Re k-epsilon, SST, Spalart-Allmaras, v2-f; LES models under Large Eddy Simulation.

tools.name: Turbulent Flow, SST (spf)
tools.description: Menter shear-stress transport two-equation model blending k-omega near walls with k-epsilon in the free stream and limiting the eddy viscosity in adverse pressure gradients; it is the general-purpose choice for external aerodynamics, airfoils, diffusers, heat sinks with separation and turbomachinery blades. It always uses a low-Re near-wall formulation (with automatic wall treatment in 6.x), so a boundary-layer mesh and wall-distance initialization are required.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Turbulent Flow > Turbulent Flow, SST (spf); API: physics().create("spf", "TurbulentFlowSST", "geom1")

parameters.name: Wall treatment
parameters.description: Automatic (default in 6.x) or Low Re.

parameters.name: Wall Distance Initialization
parameters.description: Study step solving the reciprocal wall distance before the flow (needed by SST, SA, k-omega low-Re).

parameters.name: Transition model (6.x)
parameters.description: Optional gamma-Re_theta / gamma transition models.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. y+ should be around 1 for full accuracy; the Wall Resolution plot (spf.WallResolution) in Results shows where the mesh is too coarse.

tools.name: Turbulent Flow, Spalart-Allmaras (spf)
tools.description: One-equation RANS model transporting a modified eddy viscosity, developed for aerodynamic boundary layers; cheap and robust for external flows over wings, vehicles and ship hulls with mild separation, less suited to free shear flows and internal recirculating flows. Requires wall-distance initialization and a resolved near-wall mesh.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Turbulent Flow > Turbulent Flow, Spalart-Allmaras (spf); API: physics().create("spf", "TurbulentFlowSpalartAllmaras", "geom1")

parameters.name: Wall treatment
parameters.description: Low Re (automatic).

parameters.name: Inlet turbulence
parameters.description: Modified turbulent viscosity nutilde at inlets.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. Also the base for Detached Eddy Simulation (DES) in 6.x LES/DES options.

tools.name: Large Eddy Simulation (LES RBVM / RBVMWV / Smagorinsky)
tools.description: Time-dependent turbulence interfaces that resolve the large eddies directly and model the subgrid scales through the residual-based variational multiscale method (RBVM, RBVMWV with viscosity) or a Smagorinsky model, for transitional flows, aeroacoustic sources, mixing and unsteady loads where RANS is inadequate. Needs a fine, near-isotropic mesh, small time steps (CFL < 1 in regions of interest), a spin-up period and time averaging of results (Time Average dataset).
tools.usage: Add Physics > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Large Eddy Simulation > LES RBVM (spf); API: physics().create("spf", "LESRBVM", "geom1")

parameters.name: LES model
parameters.description: RBVM | RBVMWV | Smagorinsky (via the interface variants).

parameters.name: Time-Dependent solver
parameters.description: Generalized alpha / BDF with strict steps of the convective time scale; Results While Solving and probes for monitoring.

parameters.name: Inlet perturbations
parameters.description: Synthetic turbulence at inlets (6.x) to trigger the cascade.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module (5.6+). Detached Eddy Simulation (DES) variants combine RANS near walls with LES away from them; both are far more expensive than RANS.

tools.name: Creeping Flow (spf)
tools.description: Stokes-flow interface that drops the inertial (convective) term of the Navier-Stokes equations, valid for very low Reynolds numbers (Re << 1): microfluidics, lubrication, porous-scale flows, polymer melts and viscous sediment. Linear for Newtonian fluids so it solves in one iteration, and it forms the base of the Microfluidics Module interfaces and of non-Newtonian (power law, Carreau) creeping flows.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Creeping Flow (spf); API: physics().create("spf", "CreepingFlow", "geom1")

parameters.name: Fluid Properties
parameters.description: Density, dynamic viscosity (constant, non-Newtonian model or from material).

parameters.name: Neglect inertial term
parameters.description: Interface property distinguishing it from Laminar Flow (can be toggled).

tools.notes: Core product feature. Because pressure enters only through the constraint, at least one pressure condition (outlet or Pressure Point Constraint) is required.

tools.name: Two-Phase Flow, Phase Field (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined multiphysics interface combining Laminar (or Turbulent) Flow with the Phase Field interface (pf) and the Two-Phase Flow, Phase Field coupling (tpf1): the interface between two immiscible fluids is tracked by a Cahn-Hilliard phase-field variable, which conserves mass better than level set and naturally includes surface tension and contact-angle wetting. Used for droplets, bubbles, jets, capillary filling, coating flows and sloshing; solved with Time Dependent with Phase Initialization.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Multiphase Flow > Two-Phase Flow, Phase Field > Laminar Flow; API: physics().create("spf", "LaminarFlow", "geom1"); physics().create("pf", "PhaseField", "geom1"); multiphysics().create("tpf1", "TwoPhaseFlowPhaseField", 3)

parameters.name: Fluid 1 / Fluid 2 properties
parameters.description: Set in the coupling node (from materials).

parameters.name: Surface tension coefficient
parameters.description: Library values or user defined; Marangoni effects via a temperature-dependent sigma.

parameters.name: Phase Field settings
parameters.description: Interface thickness epsilon_pf (~half the mesh size at the interface) and mobility tuning parameter chi.

parameters.name: Initial Interface / Wetted Wall (contact angle)
parameters.description: Boundary defining the initial interface; walls with contact angle theta_w.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module or Microfluidics Module. Two-Phase Flow, Level Set (already catalogued) is the alternative for topology changes with a simpler equation; Two-Phase Flow, Moving Mesh tracks a sharp interface with ALE and no topology changes. Three-Phase Flow, Phase Field extends to three fluids.

tools.name: Two-Phase Flow, Moving Mesh (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Sharp-interface two-phase (or free-surface) flow interface where the fluid-fluid boundary is an actual mesh boundary moved by the Moving Mesh (ALE) machinery; surface tension, contact angles and mass transfer enter as boundary conditions on the Free Surface / Fluid-Fluid Interface node. It gives the most accurate interface position for problems without topology change - sloshing, meniscus shapes, coating beads, rising droplets that do not break up - and needs Automatic Remeshing when the mesh distorts.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Multiphase Flow > Two-Phase Flow, Moving Mesh > Laminar Flow; or Laminar Flow + Free Surface boundary condition with Moving Mesh; API: physics("spf").create("fs1", "FreeSurface", 2); common().create("free1", "FreeDeformation")

parameters.name: Free Surface / Fluid-Fluid Interface
parameters.description: Boundary node with surface tension, external pressure and contact angle at the contact line.

parameters.name: Moving Mesh
parameters.description: Free Deformation in the fluid domains with Prescribed Mesh Displacement on fixed walls.

parameters.name: Automatic Remeshing
parameters.description: Time-dependent solver node triggering remeshing at a mesh quality threshold.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module or Microfluidics Module. Cannot handle merging/breakup; switch to Level Set or Phase Field for those.

tools.name: Level Set (ls) / Phase Field (pf) interfaces
tools.description: Stand-alone interface-tracking interfaces solving the conservative level set equation (ls: phi from 0 to 1 with reinitialization parameter and interface thickness) or the Cahn-Hilliard phase field equations (pf: phi from -1 to 1 with mobility and mixing energy). They are added automatically by the Two-Phase Flow multiphysics interfaces but can be used alone with a prescribed velocity field to track a passive interface, a solidification front or an eroding boundary, or with other couplings (Three-Phase Flow, Two-Phase Darcy).
tools.usage: Add Physics > Mathematics > Moving Interface > Level Set (ls) / Phase Field (pf); API: physics().create("ls", "LevelSet", "geom1"); physics().create("pf", "PhaseField", "geom1")

parameters.name: Level Set Model / Phase Field Model node
parameters.description: Velocity field source, reinitialization parameter gamma (ls), interface thickness epsilon (ls/pf), mobility (pf).

parameters.name: Initial Values
parameters.description: Fluid 1 / Fluid 2 assignment per domain (phi = 0/1 or -1/1).

parameters.name: Initial Interface
parameters.description: Boundary where the interface starts; Phase Initialization study step smooths it.

parameters.name: Inlet / Outlet / Wetted Wall
parameters.description: Boundary conditions with phase fraction and contact angle.

tools.notes: Core product includes Level Set and Phase Field interfaces; the coupled two-phase flow interfaces need the CFD or Microfluidics Module. Interface thickness should be about half the mesh element size at the interface; refine with Adaptive Mesh Refinement in time-dependent studies for sharp results.

tools.name: Brinkman Equations (br)
tools.description: Porous-media flow interface extending Darcy's law with viscous (Brinkman) and optional inertial (Forchheimer) terms so that velocity and pressure are continuous with free-flow regions and no-slip walls are respected; used for fast flow in high-porosity media (foams, packed beds, filters, catalyst layers, fuel-cell GDLs) and as the porous half of Free and Porous Media Flow. Turbulent-porous variants and non-isothermal coupling exist in the CFD/Heat Transfer Modules.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Fluid Flow > Porous Media and Subsurface Flow > Brinkman Equations (br); API: physics().create("br", "PorousMediaFlowBrinkman", "geom1")

parameters.name: Porous Medium node > Fluid / Porous Matrix
parameters.description: Fluid properties, porosity, permeability (isotropic or tensor, Kozeny-Carman option), Forchheimer/Ergun nonlinear drag.

parameters.name: Compressibility
parameters.description: Incompressible | Weakly compressible.

parameters.name: Inlet / Outlet / Wall / Symmetry
parameters.description: Same boundary set as Laminar Flow.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD, Porous Media Flow, Subsurface Flow, Chemical Reaction Engineering, Battery or Fuel Cell Module. Darcy's Law (already catalogued) is cheaper (pressure only) for low-permeability media where velocity boundary layers do not matter.

tools.name: Free and Porous Media Flow (fp)
tools.description: Single interface that solves Navier-Stokes in free-flow domains and the Brinkman equations in porous domains with a continuous velocity/pressure across the interface, avoiding the need for two interfaces and a coupling. Typical for flow around and through filters, membranes, packed-bed reactors with headspace, fractured rock outcrops and biological tissue with vessels.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Fluid Flow > Porous Media and Subsurface Flow > Free and Porous Media Flow (fp); API: physics().create("fp", "FreeAndPorousMediaFlow", "geom1")

parameters.name: Fluid Properties (free domains)
parameters.description: Default domain node for the free-flow region.

parameters.name: Porous Medium (porous domains)
parameters.description: Add and select porous regions with porosity, permeability and Forchheimer coefficient.

parameters.name: Turbulence (6.x)
parameters.description: Free and Porous Media Flow with k-epsilon / k-omega variants in the CFD Module.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD, Porous Media Flow, Subsurface Flow or Chemical Reaction Engineering Module. Use the Stress Jump / interface options when the Beavers-Joseph slip condition is important.

tools.name: Pipe Flow (pfl)
tools.description: Pipe Flow Module interface that solves 1D momentum and continuity along edges representing pipe networks: pressure, cross-section-averaged velocity and (with Heat Transfer in Pipes / Transport of Diluted Species in Pipes) temperature and concentration, using friction-factor correlations (Churchill, Haaland, Wood, Swamee-Jain, Stokes, user) and pressure-drop models for bends, valves, contractions, T-junctions, pumps and orifices. Suited to piping systems, district heating, cooling circuits, geothermal loops and pipelines, coupled to 3D domains via Pipe Connection features.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Fluid Flow > Single-Phase Flow > Pipe Flow (pfl); API: physics().create("pfl", "PipeFlow", "geom1")

parameters.name: Pipe Properties
parameters.description: Edge node with shape (round, square, rectangular, annular, user), diameter, surface roughness and friction model.

parameters.name: Fluid Properties
parameters.description: Density and viscosity (Newtonian or non-Newtonian).

parameters.name: Inlet / Outlet / Pressure / Volumetric flow rate
parameters.description: Point boundary conditions at pipe ends.

parameters.name: Bend / Valve / T-Junction / Pump / Contraction-Expansion / Orifice
parameters.description: Point features adding loss coefficients or pump curves.

parameters.name: Wall Heat Transfer (Heat Transfer in Pipes)
parameters.description: External film resistance and wall layers for htp.

tools.notes: Requires the Pipe Flow Module. Water Hammer (whtd) is the compressible transient variant; Pipe Acoustics handles acoustic waves in pipes; Pipe Mechanics gives the structural response. The Pipe dataset renders results as 3D tubes.

tools.name: High Mach Number Flow (hmnf)
tools.description: Compressible flow interface for transonic, supersonic and hypersonic regimes solving the fully coupled Navier-Stokes (or Euler) equations with the energy equation for an ideal gas, using consistent stabilisation and shock capturing; laminar, k-epsilon, Spalart-Allmaras and SST variants exist. Applications: nozzles, supersonic inlets, shock tubes, projectiles and high-speed aerodynamics.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Fluid Flow > High Mach Number Flow > High Mach Number Flow, Laminar / k-epsilon / SST (hmnf); API: physics().create("hmnf", "HighMachNumberFlow", "geom1")

parameters.name: Fluid node
parameters.description: Ideal gas with cp, ratio of specific heats, viscosity (Sutherland) and conductivity.

parameters.name: Inlet types
parameters.description: Characteristics-based (Mach number, static/total pressure, temperature), supersonic inlet.

parameters.name: Outlet / Hybrid Outlet
parameters.description: Supersonic or subsonic outlet with pressure.

parameters.name: Pseudo time stepping / initial Mach
parameters.description: Initialise with a uniform flow and ramp the Mach number for convergence.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. Mesh shocks with adaptive refinement (Adaptation in the study step) and use a fully coupled solver; the standard spf interface with Compressible flow (Ma < 0.3) option suffices for low-speed compressibility.

tools.name: Rotating Machinery, Fluid Flow (Frozen Rotor)
tools.description: Laminar/turbulent flow interfaces (Fluid Flow > Rotating Machinery, Fluid Flow) for mixers, pumps, turbines and fans: rotor domains are placed in a Rotating Domain (moving mesh) separated from the stator by an assembly pair, and the Frozen Rotor study computes a quasi-steady solution in the rotating frame (rotor fixed at one angle, with centrifugal and Coriolis terms) as an inexpensive approximation or as the initial condition for a full Time Dependent sliding-mesh run. The Mixer Module adds impeller and vessel part libraries, mixing-plane options and free-surface vessel flows.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Fluid Flow > Rotating Machinery, Fluid Flow > Laminar Flow (spf with Rotating Domain); Study > Frozen Rotor / Time Dependent; API: physics().create("spf", "LaminarFlow", "geom1"); common().create("rot1", "RotatingDomain"); study.create("frot", "FrozenRotor")

parameters.name: Rotating Domain
parameters.description: Rotor domains and rotational speed.

parameters.name: Continuity pair feature (spf)
parameters.description: Flow continuity across the rotor-stator sliding interface (identity pair).

parameters.name: Frozen Rotor study
parameters.description: Stationary in the rotating frame; Frozen Rotor with Initialization for turbulent cases.

parameters.name: Rotating Wall / Interior Wall
parameters.description: Wall conditions that follow the rotation.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module or Mixer Module. Frozen Rotor results depend on the chosen rotor angle; for periodic-in-time quantities run the Time Dependent study from the frozen-rotor solution for a few revolutions.

tools.name: Thin-Film Flow, Shell (tffs)
tools.description: Boundary interface solving the Reynolds equation for the pressure in a thin lubricating or gas film between two surfaces, with squeeze-film and slide-film damping, gas rarefaction (Knudsen-number corrections), cavitation and elastohydrodynamic options; Thin-Film Flow, Domain and Edge variants cover other dimensions. Used for MEMS squeeze-film damping (accelerometers, micromirrors), journal/thrust bearings (with Hydrodynamic Bearing), seals and lubricated contacts.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Fluid Flow > Thin-Film Flow > Thin-Film Flow, Shell (tffs); API: physics().create("tffs", "ThinFilmFlowShell", "geom1")

parameters.name: Fluid-Film Properties
parameters.description: Film thickness (from geometry, expression or structural displacement), wall/base velocities, viscosity, gas model, rarefaction.

parameters.name: Border / Inlet / Outlet
parameters.description: Edge conditions on the film boundary (ambient pressure, flow).

parameters.name: Fluid-Film Damping / Thin-Film Damping (multiphysics)
parameters.description: Couples film pressure to Solid Mechanics or Shell for damped eigenfrequencies.

tools.notes: Requires the MEMS Module or CFD Module (Hydrodynamic Bearing in the Rotordynamics Module). Frequency-domain studies give complex stiffness/damping of the film directly. The API type string in this entry could not be confirmed in the COMSOL 6.4 registry; confirm it with Model Builder > File > Save As > Model File for Java.

tools.name: Bubbly Flow / Mixture Model / Euler-Euler Model
tools.description: Dispersed multiphase flow interfaces of the CFD Module that do not track individual interfaces: Bubbly Flow (bf) for low gas fractions of bubbles in liquid (aerators, bubble columns), Mixture Model (mm) for particles/droplets/bubbles of a dispersed phase with slip velocity models (Schiller-Naumann, Hadamard-Rybczynski, Haider-Levenspiel) and interphase mass transfer, and Euler-Euler Model (ee) solving momentum equations for both phases for dense suspensions and fluidized beds. Laminar and turbulent variants exist.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Fluid Flow > Multiphase Flow > Bubbly Flow (bf) / Mixture Model (mm) / Euler-Euler Model (ee), Laminar or Turbulent; API: physics().create("mm", "LaminarMixtureModel", "geom1") (type names vary per variant)

parameters.name: Mixture / Phase Properties
parameters.description: Continuous and dispersed phase densities, viscosities, particle diameter, slip model, maximum packing.

parameters.name: Gas Boundary Condition / Inlet / Outlet / Wall
parameters.description: Phase fluxes and volume fractions at boundaries.

parameters.name: Mass Transfer
parameters.description: Interphase mass transfer (evaporation, dissolution, reactions).

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module. Phase Transport (phtr) with Phase Transport Mixture Model (6.x) extends the mixture model to any number of phases; Particle Tracing for Fluid Flow is the Lagrangian alternative for dilute particles.

tools.name: Shallow Water Equations (swe)
tools.description: Depth-averaged flow interface solving the Saint-Venant equations for water depth and horizontal velocity over a bathymetry, with bottom friction (Manning/Chezy), wind stress, Coriolis force and wetting/drying; used for rivers, floods, estuaries, dam breaks, tsunamis and harbour hydrodynamics in 1D and 2D. Time-dependent by nature, with the Time Explicit variant using discontinuous Galerkin for large domains.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Fluid Flow > Shallow Water Equations > Shallow Water Equations, Time Explicit (swe); API: physics().create("swe", "ShallowWaterEquationsTimeExplicit", "geom1")

parameters.name: Bathymetry
parameters.description: Bottom elevation expression (e.g. from an Elevation function).

parameters.name: Initial water depth / velocity
parameters.description: Initial Values node.

parameters.name: Inflow / Outflow / Wall / Open boundary
parameters.description: Discharge, depth or characteristic-based boundary conditions.

parameters.name: Friction model
parameters.description: Manning coefficient or Chezy.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module (5.6+). Explicit time stepping is CFL limited; the solver picks the step automatically from the mesh and wave speed.

tools.name: Fluid Properties (spf)
tools.description: Default domain node of the single-phase flow interfaces holding density and dynamic viscosity (from material, user defined, or non-Newtonian models: Power law, Carreau, Bingham-Papanastasiou, Herschel-Bulkley, Casson, Cross, thixotropic in the Polymer Flow Module), plus turbulence-model parameters and the mixing-length limit. Add extra nodes when different domains have different fluids (multi-fluid but single-phase, e.g. gas region and liquid region separated by a membrane).
tools.usage: Physics > Laminar Flow > Fluid Properties (fp1 default); API: physics("spf").feature("fp1").set("mu_mat", "userdef"); set("mu", ...)

parameters.name: rho / mu
parameters.description: Density and dynamic viscosity (From material or User defined).

parameters.name: Constitutive relation (6.x)
parameters.description: Newtonian | Inelastic non-Newtonian (Power law, Carreau, Bingham...).

parameters.name: Reference pressure / temperature
parameters.description: Interface-level reference values used for compressible and gas-law densities.

tools.notes: Core product includes Power law and Carreau; other non-Newtonian and viscoelastic (Oldroyd-B, Giesekus...) models need the Polymer Flow Module. Temperature-dependent properties come through the Model Inputs section when coupled to heat transfer.

tools.name: Symmetry (fluid flow)
tools.description: Boundary condition for symmetry planes of the flow: zero normal velocity and zero tangential viscous stress (slip without friction), which is also what a free-slip wall or the far boundary of an external flow needs. Use it to halve models; for turbulence models the turbulence quantities get zero-flux conditions automatically.
tools.usage: Physics > Laminar Flow > Symmetry (sym1); API: physics("spf").create("sym1", "Symmetry", 2)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Symmetry planes.

tools.notes: Core product feature. The Wall node with Slip condition is equivalent; the axis of a 2D axisymmetric model gets an automatic Axial Symmetry node.

tools.name: Open Boundary (fluid flow)
tools.description: Boundary condition for exterior boundaries where the flow direction is unknown (may enter or leave): it prescribes the normal stress (pressure) with no viscous stress and lets the velocity adjust, suitable for the far field of natural convection, plumes, jets in a large reservoir and outlets with backflow. Compared with Outlet it does not suppress inflow, so it is more permissive but can be less stable; combine with the flow direction constraint options when needed.
tools.usage: Physics > Laminar Flow > Open Boundary (open1); API: physics("spf").create("open1", "OpenBoundary", 2)

parameters.name: Boundary condition type
parameters.description: Normal stress f0 or No viscous stress.

parameters.name: f0
parameters.description: Normal stress (pressure) at the boundary, e.g. 0 or hydrostatic.

tools.notes: Core product feature. Pair with Heat Transfer > Open Boundary and Transport > Open Boundary for the scalar fields on the same boundaries.

tools.name: Periodic Flow Condition
tools.description: Boundary condition making velocity (and pressure up to a prescribed pressure difference) periodic between a source and a destination boundary, so a repeating channel section, a heat-exchanger unit cell or a fully developed flow can be computed on one period with a given pressure drop driving the flow. Mesh both boundaries identically (Copy Face) for accuracy.
tools.usage: Physics > Laminar Flow > Periodic Flow Condition (pfc1); API: physics("spf").create("pfc1", "PeriodicFlowCondition", 2)

parameters.name: Source / Destination
parameters.description: The two boundaries (automatic detection by default).

parameters.name: Pressure difference p_src - p_dst
parameters.description: Driving pressure drop over the period (0 for pure periodicity).

tools.notes: Core product feature. With a periodic condition the pressure level is undetermined unless a Pressure Point Constraint or an outlet exists elsewhere.

tools.name: Pressure Point Constraint
tools.description: Point feature fixing the pressure at one vertex, needed to remove the pressure null space in closed cavities (lid-driven cavity, natural convection in an enclosure, all-wall domains) or in periodic flows where no boundary sets the pressure level. Without it the linear system is singular and the solver reports a zero pivot or drifting pressure.
tools.usage: Physics > Laminar Flow > Points > Pressure Point Constraint (ppc1); API: physics("spf").create("ppc1", "PressurePointConstraint", 0)

parameters.name: p0
parameters.description: Pressure value at the point (usually 0).

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: One vertex, preferably at a wall corner away from regions of interest.

tools.notes: Core product feature. In weakly compressible closed cavities the total mass, not the pressure, should be constrained - use the interface's 'Reference pressure level' plus a Global Constraint on the integrated density if precision matters.

tools.name: Fan / Interior Fan / Screen / Grille
tools.description: Lumped boundary conditions for devices in ducts and enclosures: Fan (exterior inlet/outlet with a static pressure curve p(Q), from a table or fan curve library) and Interior Fan (interior boundary with a pressure jump curve) model axial/centrifugal fans without meshing blades; Screen (wire gauze, perforated plate, mesh) and Grille (exterior with loss coefficient) add a pressure drop and flow deflection through resistance coefficients. Essential for electronics-cooling and HVAC models.
tools.usage: Physics > Laminar/Turbulent Flow > Fan (fan1) / Interior Fan (ifan1) / Screen (scr1) / Grille (grl1); API: physics("spf").create("fan1", "Fan", 2); create("ifan1", "InteriorFan", 2); create("scr1", "Screen", 2)

parameters.name: Fan curve
parameters.description: Static pressure vs flow rate: linear, from table (interpolation function) or fan library entry.

parameters.name: Flow direction / swirl
parameters.description: Inlet or outlet type, optional swirl velocity.

parameters.name: Screen type / solidity
parameters.description: Wire gauze, square mesh, perforated plate with solidity and loss coefficient K.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module or Heat Transfer Module. Interior Fan needs a boundary inside the fluid domain (add a partition face). The Fan defined by a fan curve makes the problem nonlinear; ramp with an auxiliary sweep if convergence is poor.

tools.name: Boundary Stress
tools.description: General traction boundary condition prescribing the total stress vector (or only its normal component) on an exterior boundary, used for open boundaries with a known stress, free surfaces with surface tension effects in the Microfluidics Module, and to impose a pressure while allowing tangential slip. Outlet with 'Normal stress' and Open Boundary are special cases.
tools.usage: Physics > Laminar Flow > Boundary Stress (bs1); API: physics("spf").create("bs1", "BoundaryStress", 2)

parameters.name: Boundary condition
parameters.description: General stress | Normal stress | Normal stress, normal flow.

parameters.name: F / f0
parameters.description: Stress vector or normal stress value.

tools.notes: Core product feature. Sign convention: the stress is the traction on the fluid, so a positive outlet pressure p corresponds to f0 = -p.

tools.name: Wall treatment / wall functions (turbulence)
tools.description: Interface-level setting and Wall-node behaviour of the RANS interfaces controlling how the near-wall region is modelled: Wall functions (standard, with a lift-off giving the wall distance delta_w+ where the log law is applied; robust on coarse meshes), Low Re (integrates to the wall, needs y+ ~ 1) and Automatic (6.x, switches locally between the two based on the mesh). The Wall node itself offers No slip, Slip, Moving wall/Sliding wall, Leaking wall and, for rough walls, a sand-grain roughness height that modifies the wall function.
tools.usage: Turbulent Flow settings > Turbulence > Wall treatment: Wall functions | Low Re | Automatic; Wall node > Wall roughness; API: physics("spf").prop("TurbulenceModelProperty").set("WallTreatment", "WallFunctions"|"LowRe"|"Automatic")

parameters.name: WallTreatment
parameters.description: WallFunctions | LowRe | Automatic.

parameters.name: Wall roughness
parameters.description: Smooth | Rough with equivalent sand roughness ks and roughness parameter Cs.

parameters.name: Wall condition
parameters.description: NoSlip | Slip | MovingWall | SlidingWall | LeakingWall.

tools.notes: Requires the CFD Module for turbulence. Check spf.Delta_wPlus (wall lift-off in viscous units) after solving: values much above 11.06 mean the mesh is too coarse for wall functions to be accurate near the wall.

tools.name: Linearized Navier-Stokes, Frequency Domain (lnsf)
tools.description: Acoustics Module interface solving the linearized compressible Navier-Stokes equations (pressure, velocity and temperature perturbations) on top of a background mean flow from a CFD solution, capturing viscous and thermal losses, convection and flow-acoustic interaction: mufflers with flow, liners, flow ducts, aeroacoustic transmission loss, and detailed microphone/transducer modelling with flow. A Transient variant exists, and the Background Fluid Flow Coupling multiphysics node maps the CFD solution (with a dedicated Mapping study).
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Aeroacoustics > Linearized Navier-Stokes, Frequency Domain (lnsf); API: physics().create("lnsf", "LinearizedNavierStokesFrequency", "geom1")

parameters.name: Linearized Navier-Stokes Model
parameters.description: Background mean flow variables (p0, u0, T0 from the CFD study via the coupling), fluid properties, stabilization.

parameters.name: Wall / Impedance / Pressure / Velocity / Port (6.x)
parameters.description: Boundary conditions including slip/no-slip and isothermal/adiabatic walls.

parameters.name: Gradient term suppression / stabilization
parameters.description: Numerical options for stable convected acoustics.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Linearized Euler (lef) neglects viscosity and conduction and is cheaper for high-Reynolds-number flow ducts; Linearized Potential Flow / Convected Wave Equation handle irrotational background flows.

tools.name: Ray Acoustics (rac)
tools.description: Geometrical (high-frequency) acoustics interface tracing sound rays through rooms and outdoor environments with reflection/absorption at walls (specular, diffuse, mixed with frequency-dependent absorption coefficients), atmospheric attenuation, and graded media, producing impulse responses at receivers, reverberation time, energy decay curves and sound pressure levels per octave band. Used for room acoustics, concert halls, auditoria, outdoor noise propagation and underwater acoustics at high frequency where FEM is too expensive.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Geometrical Acoustics > Ray Acoustics (rac); Study > Ray Tracing; API: physics().create("rac", "RayAcoustics", "geom1")

parameters.name: Medium Properties
parameters.description: Speed of sound, density, attenuation (or the built-in atmosphere/ocean models).

parameters.name: Release from Point / Grid / Boundary with power and directivity
parameters.description: Sources with frequency bands (octave/1/3 octave) and directivity patterns.

parameters.name: Wall
parameters.description: Absorption coefficient (per band), specular/diffuse scattering coefficient.

parameters.name: Receiver 2D/3D dataset
parameters.description: Sphere/circle collecting rays to build impulse response and energy decay plots.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Results: Ray Trajectories, Receiver datasets with Impulse Response plot and Energy Decay attribute, reverberation time evaluation. The domain need not be meshed for rays if 'Compute in unmeshed domains' is used, but walls must be geometry boundaries.

tools.name: Poroelastic Waves (pelw)
tools.description: Biot-theory interface solving coupled fluid pressure and solid displacement waves in fluid-saturated porous elastic materials (rock, foams, fibrous absorbers, bone, sediments) including viscous and thermal losses (Biot-Allard), in frequency domain and eigenfrequency studies. It couples to Pressure Acoustics and Solid Mechanics through the Acoustic-Porous Boundary and Porous-Structure Boundary multiphysics nodes for absorbers on walls, mufflers with porous liners and seismic problems.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Poroelastic Waves > Poroelastic Waves (pelw); API: physics().create("pelw", "PoroelasticWavesSinglePhysics", "geom1")

parameters.name: Poroelastic Material
parameters.description: Porous matrix (drained E, nu, density, porosity, tortuosity, flow resistivity, viscous/thermal characteristic lengths) and saturating fluid properties; Biot or Biot-Allard model.

parameters.name: Fixed Constraint / Prescribed Displacement / Sound Hard / Pressure
parameters.description: Boundary conditions for both fields.

parameters.name: Multiphysics couplings
parameters.description: Acoustic-Porous Boundary (acpr-pelw), Porous-Structure Boundary (pelw-solid).

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. For rigid-frame absorbers the cheaper Poroacoustics domain node in Pressure Acoustics (Delany-Bazley-Miki, Johnson-Champoux-Allard...) is usually sufficient.

tools.name: Pressure Acoustics, Boundary Elements (pabe)
tools.description: BEM formulation of the Helmholtz equation that meshes only surfaces and radiates to infinity automatically (no PML, no air mesh), for exterior radiation and scattering from loudspeakers, transducers, vehicles and sonar targets at moderate frequencies; couples to FEM Pressure Acoustics (for interior/complex regions) and to Solid Mechanics/Shell (Acoustic-Structure Boundary) through hybrid FEM-BEM couplings. The BEM matrices are dense but compressed with the adaptive cross approximation.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Pressure Acoustics > Pressure Acoustics, Boundary Elements (pabe); API: physics().create("pabe", "PressureAcousticsBoundaryElements", "geom1")

parameters.name: Pressure Acoustics (infinite void)
parameters.description: Fluid of the unbounded exterior; symmetry/infinite baffle options.

parameters.name: Sound Hard / Normal Acceleration / Impedance / Pressure
parameters.description: Boundary conditions on BEM surfaces.

parameters.name: Exterior field
parameters.description: Far-field pressure is available directly at any point (pabe.p_ext).

parameters.name: Solver
parameters.description: Iterative GMRES with BEM preconditioning is set up automatically.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Mesh about 6 elements per wavelength on the surfaces; the Burton-Miller formulation avoids spurious resonances. For very large problems the FEM interface with PML may still be faster.

tools.name: Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit (pate) / Elastic Waves, Time Explicit (elte)
tools.description: Discontinuous Galerkin (dG-FEM) time-domain interfaces with explicit Runge-Kutta stepping for large, transient wave propagation problems spanning many wavelengths: pulse propagation, ultrasound imaging and NDT, seismic wave propagation, impulse responses of rooms, and the Piezoelectric Waves, Time Explicit variant for transducers. Memory-lean and scalable (matrix-free), with absorbing layers instead of PMLs; couple pate and elte with the Acoustic-Structure Boundary, Time Explicit node.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Pressure Acoustics > Pressure Acoustics, Time Explicit (pate); Elastic Waves > Elastic Waves, Time Explicit (elte); API: physics().create("pate", "PressureAcousticsTimeExplicit", "geom1"); physics().create("elte", "ElasticWavesTimeExplicit", "geom1")

parameters.name: Domain material models
parameters.description: Fluid (pate), Elastic Material / anisotropic / attenuation (elte).

parameters.name: Sources
parameters.description: Background/incident wave, normal velocity, pressure, point source with time-dependent signals (Gaussian pulse functions).

parameters.name: Absorbing Layers
parameters.description: Definitions node that damps outgoing waves at the boundary (used instead of PML).

parameters.name: Mesh / time step
parameters.description: Coarser mesh than FEM (about 1.5 elements per wavelength with quartic elements); CFL-controlled step chosen automatically.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module (elte also in the Structural Mechanics Module). Results at fixed points need the Time Explicit interfaces' probe support; use Time to Frequency FFT for spectra.

tools.name: Convected Wave Equation, Time Explicit (cwe) / Linearized Potential Flow (lpff)
tools.description: Aeroacoustics interfaces for sound in a moving fluid without solving the full linearized Navier-Stokes system: Convected Wave Equation, Time Explicit (cwe) solves a dG time-domain wave equation with a stationary background flow for large transient duct/jet-noise problems, and Linearized Potential Flow, Frequency Domain / Transient (lpff, lpft) solves the potential formulation valid for irrotational, isentropic mean flows (aircraft fuselage/engine intake noise, flow ducts). Compressible Potential Flow (cpf) supplies the background flow.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Aeroacoustics > Convected Wave Equation, Time Explicit (cwe) / Linearized Potential Flow, Frequency Domain (lpff); API: physics().create("cwe", "ConvectedWaveEquation", "geom1")

parameters.name: Background mean flow
parameters.description: User expressions or coupled from Compressible Potential Flow / CFD.

parameters.name: Sources / boundaries
parameters.description: Sound hard wall, normal velocity, impedance, absorbing layers.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Choose lnsf/lef when vortical mean flow and shear layers matter, cwe/lpff when the flow is close to potential.

tools.name: Pipe Acoustics, Frequency Domain (pafd) / Transient (patd)
tools.description: 1D acoustics along edges of pipe networks (fluid-filled pipes with elastic walls) computing pressure and velocity waves with wall compliance, damping and fittings, in the frequency domain (transmission, resonances of exhaust systems, hydraulic lines, organ pipes) or time domain (water hammer-like acoustic transients). Couples to 3D Pressure Acoustics through pipe-to-domain connection features.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Acoustics > Pipe Acoustics > Pipe Acoustics, Frequency Domain (pafd) / Transient (patd); API: physics().create("pafd", "FrequencyPipeAcoustics", "geom1")

parameters.name: Fluid Properties / Pipe Properties
parameters.description: Fluid speed of sound and density, pipe shape, diameter, wall thickness, Young's modulus (wall compliance).

parameters.name: Pressure / Velocity / Closed / Open / End Impedance
parameters.description: Point conditions at pipe ends.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module and the Pipe Flow Module.

tools.name: Acoustic-Structure Interaction (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined interface (Acoustics > Acoustic-Structure Interaction > Acoustic-Solid Interaction, Frequency Domain / Transient, Acoustic-Shell Interaction, Acoustic-Piezoelectric Interaction, Thermoviscous Acoustic-Structure Interaction) that adds Pressure Acoustics, Solid Mechanics (or Shell/Piezo) and the Acoustic-Structure Boundary coupling (asb1) on the shared boundaries: the fluid pressure loads the structure and the structural normal acceleration drives the fluid. Used for loudspeakers, transducers, hearing aids, sonar, fluid-loaded plates, tanks and vibro-acoustic transmission.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Acoustics > Acoustic-Structure Interaction > Acoustic-Solid Interaction, Frequency Domain; API: physics().create("acpr", "PressureAcoustics", "geom1"); physics().create("solid", "SolidMechanics", "geom1"); multiphysics().create("asb1", "AcousticStructureBoundary", 2)

parameters.name: Acoustic-Structure Boundary
parameters.description: Selection of interface boundaries (automatic); option for interior boundaries with pressure jump (thin structures).

parameters.name: Studies
parameters.description: Frequency Domain (response), Eigenfrequency (coupled modes, complex), Time Dependent, Frequency Domain, Modal.

parameters.name: Solver
parameters.description: Fully coupled direct or the acoustics-structure segregated iterative setup generated automatically.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module (Structural Mechanics Module for shells). The Acoustic-Structure Boundary coupling entry in the earlier chunk documents the node; Aeroacoustic-Structure and Thermoviscous Acoustic-Structure Boundary are analogous couplings.

tools.name: Impedance (acoustics)
tools.description: Pressure Acoustics boundary condition p = Zi * (normal velocity) with a specific acoustic impedance Zi given by a user expression or built-in models: RCL circuit, physiological (human skin, ear drum, ear canal, Zwislocki coupler), waveguide end impedance (flanged/unflanged pipe), porous layer backed by a wall, characteristic impedance rho*c (simple absorbing condition), and the Delany-Bazley/Miki absorber models. It is the standard way to represent absorbing walls, liners, ear simulators and lumped terminations.
tools.usage: Physics > Pressure Acoustics > Impedance (imp1); API: physics("acpr").create("imp1", "Impedance", 2); set("ImpedanceModel", "UserDefined"|"RCL"|"Physiological"|"WaveguideEnd"|"PorousLayer"|"CharacteristicImpedance")

parameters.name: ImpedanceModel
parameters.description: UserDefined | RCL | Physiological | WaveguideEnd | PorousLayer | CharacteristicImpedance.

parameters.name: Zi
parameters.description: Impedance expression (Pa*s/m), e.g. 1.2*343*(1+0.2i).

parameters.name: Model parameters
parameters.description: Rac, Cac, Lac for RCL; radius for waveguide end; thickness and flow resistivity for porous layer.

tools.notes: Core product includes the user-defined impedance; the model library of impedances needs the Acoustics Module. Interior Impedance / Interior Perforated Plate are the two-sided interior versions.

tools.name: Port (acoustics)
tools.description: Waveguide port for Pressure Acoustics (and Thermoviscous/LNS in 6.x) that excites and absorbs propagating duct modes on a boundary: analytic modes for circular, rectangular and slit ducts, numeric modes from a Boundary Mode Analysis, or user-defined; ports give the transmission loss, reflection and S-parameter-like scattering matrix between inlets and outlets of mufflers, silencers, filters and horn throats, and the Port Sweep study option computes the full matrix automatically.
tools.usage: Physics > Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain > Port (port1); API: physics("acpr").create("port1", "Port", 2); set("PortType", "Circular"|"Rectangular"|"Slit"|"Numeric"|"UserDefined")

parameters.name: PortType
parameters.description: Circular | Rectangular | Slit | Numeric | UserDefined.

parameters.name: Mode numbers
parameters.description: Azimuthal/radial or (m, n) indices of the excited mode.

parameters.name: Incident wave amplitude / Activate port sweep
parameters.description: Excitation amplitude and automatic sweep over ports.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. Ports absorb only the listed modes; above the cut-on frequency of higher modes add ports for them or use a PML instead.

tools.name: Background Pressure Field
tools.description: Domain node in Pressure Acoustics that splits the total pressure into a prescribed background field (plane wave, cylindrical wave, spherical wave, user-defined, or a field from another solution) plus the scattered field that is solved for - the acoustic scattered-field formulation for scattering off objects (sonar targets, hearing-aid shells, diffusers), incident-wave excitation of transducers, and radiation-force computations. The PML then absorbs only the scattered field.
tools.usage: Physics > Pressure Acoustics > Background Pressure Field (bpf1); API: physics("acpr").create("bpf1", "BackgroundPressureField", 3)

parameters.name: Pressure field type
parameters.description: PlaneWave | CylindricalWave | SphericalWave | UserDefined | FromModal/other solution.

parameters.name: p0, direction, wave number
parameters.description: Amplitude, propagation direction vector, and k (from the interface or user).

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Domains in which the background field is defined (typically all fluid domains including PML).

tools.notes: Core product feature. Exterior Field Calculation on a surface around the scatterer gives the far-field scattered pressure and directivity.

tools.name: Sound Hard Boundary (Wall) / Sound Soft Boundary
tools.description: The two basic Pressure Acoustics boundary conditions: Sound Hard Boundary (Wall), the default exterior condition, sets the normal acceleration to zero (rigid, perfectly reflecting wall, or a symmetry plane); Sound Soft Boundary sets p = 0 (pressure release surface such as a free water surface seen from below, or an antisymmetry plane). Interior Sound Hard Boundary (Wall) places a thin rigid baffle inside the domain.
tools.usage: Physics > Pressure Acoustics > Sound Hard Boundary (Wall) (shb1 default) / Sound Soft Boundary (ssb1); API: physics("acpr").create("ssb1", "SoundSoft", 2); create("shb2", "SoundHard", 2)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Boundaries with the condition.

tools.notes: Core product features. Truly open boundaries need a radiation condition (Plane/Spherical Wave Radiation), a Matched Boundary, a Port or a PML rather than either of these.

tools.name: Normal Acceleration / Normal Velocity / Normal Displacement
tools.description: Pressure Acoustics boundary sources prescribing the inward normal acceleration a_n (or velocity/displacement, which are equivalent in the frequency domain by factors of i*omega), representing a vibrating piston, membrane or transducer face when the structure is not modelled. With the Acoustic-Structure Boundary coupling the same quantity is taken from the structural solution instead. Also used as the excitation of ports and horns.
tools.usage: Physics > Pressure Acoustics > Normal Acceleration (nacc1) / Normal Velocity (nvel1) / Normal Displacement (ndisp1); API: physics("acpr").create("nacc1", "NormalAcceleration", 2); set("an", ...)

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: Inward acceleration (scalar along normal) or an acceleration vector.

parameters.name: an / vn / dn
parameters.description: Prescribed value or expression, e.g. 1[m/s^2] or a piston profile.

tools.notes: Core product features. In transient acoustics prescribe a time-dependent function (e.g. a Gaussian pulse or a tone burst) for the acceleration.

tools.name: Plane Wave Radiation / Spherical & Cylindrical Wave Radiation
tools.description: First/second-order absorbing (non-reflecting) boundary conditions of Pressure Acoustics that let outgoing plane, cylindrical or spherical waves leave the domain with little reflection and can carry an Incident Pressure Field subnode to inject an incoming wave. They are cheaper than a PML and adequate when the wave hits the boundary close to normally (plane) or the boundary is a sphere/cylinder centred on the source; use a PML when waves arrive at grazing angles or at low frequency.
tools.usage: Physics > Pressure Acoustics > Radiation Conditions > Plane Wave Radiation (pwr1) / Spherical Wave Radiation (swr1) / Cylindrical Wave Radiation (cwr1); API: physics("acpr").create("pwr1", "PlaneWaveRadiation", 2); pwr1.create("ipf1", "IncidentPressureField", 2)

parameters.name: Radius / source location
parameters.description: For spherical/cylindrical conditions: the centre (r0) the wave originates from.

parameters.name: Incident Pressure Field subnode
parameters.description: Plane wave (amplitude, direction) or user-defined incident field entering through the boundary.

tools.notes: Core product features. The Matched Boundary condition is the waveguide-mode version for ducts; Absorbing Layers exist for the time-explicit interfaces.

tools.name: Monopole Point Source / Dipole Point Source
tools.description: Point features in Pressure Acoustics injecting a volume flow rate (monopole, given by flow rate, power, or a spherical-wave amplitude) or a dipole moment at a vertex, to represent small sources such as a pulsating sphere, a loudspeaker in the compact limit, or a test source for room responses. Domain-level Monopole Domain Source / Dipole Domain Source distribute sources over a volume, and edge/point versions exist in 2D axisymmetry.
tools.usage: Physics > Pressure Acoustics > Points > Monopole Point Source (mps1); API: physics("acpr").create("mps1", "MonopolePointSource", 0); set("Type", "FlowRate"|"Power"|"UserDefined")

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: FlowRate (Qs, m^3/s) | Power (Prms, W) | UserDefined amplitude.

parameters.name: Qs / Prms
parameters.description: Source strength.

tools.notes: Core product features. The field is singular at the point; evaluate sound pressure level at a distance. In room acoustics use the power option so SPL matches a source of known power.

tools.name: Interior Perforated Plate / Interior Impedance
tools.description: Interior boundary conditions of Pressure Acoustics that relate the pressure jump across a thin interior surface to the normal velocity through a transfer impedance: Interior Impedance takes a user expression, while Interior Perforated Plate computes it from hole diameter, plate thickness, porosity, end corrections and flow/thermoviscous loss models for perforates, micro-perforated panels and grilles - the standard muffler and liner components.
tools.usage: Physics > Pressure Acoustics > Interior Conditions > Interior Perforated Plate (ipp1) / Interior Impedance (iimp1); API: physics("acpr").create("ipp1", "InteriorPerforatedPlate", 2)

parameters.name: Hole diameter dh / plate thickness tp / porosity
parameters.description: Geometric data of the perforate.

parameters.name: Model
parameters.description: Circular holes with end correction and discharge coefficient options; MPP thermoviscous model.

parameters.name: Zi (Interior Impedance)
parameters.description: Transfer impedance expression.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. The interior boundary must be a real boundary in the geometry (partition the domain).

tools.name: Narrow Region Acoustics / Poroacoustics
tools.description: Domain material models of Pressure Acoustics that include losses without solving thermoviscous acoustics: Narrow Region Acoustics adds homogenised viscous and thermal boundary-layer losses for waveguides of constant cross-section (slits, circular tubes, rectangular ducts, equilateral triangles, or a user duct with hydraulic radius) - hearing aids, mobile-phone ports, MEMS microphones; Poroacoustics models rigid-frame porous absorbers with the Delany-Bazley, Miki, Qunli, Wood, Johnson-Champoux-Allard(-Lafarge/-Pride), Attenborough, Zwikker-Kosten or Williams models from flow resistivity and porous parameters.
tools.usage: Physics > Pressure Acoustics > Narrow Region Acoustics (nra1) / Poroacoustics (pa1); API: physics("acpr").create("nra1", "NarrowRegionAcoustics", 3); create("pa1", "Poroacoustics", 3)

parameters.name: Duct type (nra)
parameters.description: Slit | Circular duct | Rectangular duct | Equilateral triangle | User defined (hydraulic radius).

parameters.name: Poroacoustic model (pa)
parameters.description: DelanyBazley | Miki | JCA | JCAL | Zwikker-Kosten | ... with flow resistivity Rf, porosity, tortuosity and characteristic lengths.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. When the boundary layers occupy most of the cross-section (very narrow ducts) or the geometry is not a uniform duct, use Thermoviscous Acoustics instead.

tools.name: Exterior Field Calculation
tools.description: Boundary node in Pressure Acoustics that applies the Helmholtz-Kirchhoff integral on a closed surface around the sources/scatterers to compute the pressure at any exterior point (including the far field) - variables acpr.efc1.pext, sound pressure level acpr.efc1.Lp_pext and directivity - used by the Radiation Pattern plots and Directivity plot for loudspeakers, transducers and scattering targets. Symmetry planes (infinite baffles) can be declared so a half model yields the full pattern.
tools.usage: Physics > Pressure Acoustics, Frequency Domain > Exterior Field Calculation (efc1); API: physics("acpr").create("efc1", "ExteriorFieldCalculation", 2)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Closed surface (inside the PML, outside all sources).

parameters.name: Type of integral (IntType)
parameters.description: FullIntegral (Helmholtz-Kirchhoff integral over a closed surface) | IntegralApproximation (faster approximation for far-field evaluation).

parameters.name: Symmetry / infinite baffle
parameters.description: Symmetry planes in x, y, z with sound hard/soft type.

tools.notes: Requires the Acoustics Module. The surface must be inside the physical (non-PML) domain and enclose all sources; results are valid only outside it. Verified against COMSOL 6.4: the variables are acpr.efc1.pext and acpr.efc1.Lp_pext, and the integral type is set with IntType = FullIntegral | IntegralApproximation.

tools.name: Periodic Condition (acoustics)
tools.description: Source-destination periodic condition for Pressure Acoustics and the other acoustics interfaces with Continuity, Antiperiodicity, Floquet periodicity (given k-vector for oblique incidence on periodic structures such as metamaterial panels, perforated screens, sonic crystals) and Cyclic symmetry (sector angle and azimuthal mode number for rotationally periodic devices like fans or transducer arrays).
tools.usage: Physics > Pressure Acoustics > Periodic Condition (pc1); API: physics("acpr").create("pc1", "PeriodicCondition", 2); set("PeriodicType", "Continuity"|"Antiperiodicity"|"Floquet"|"CyclicSymmetry")

parameters.name: PeriodicType
parameters.description: Continuity | Antiperiodicity | Floquet | CyclicSymmetry.

parameters.name: kFloquet / azimuthal mode number
parameters.description: Wave vector or mode number for the phase shift.

tools.notes: Core product feature (Floquet/cyclic types with the Acoustics Module). Copy the mesh between source and destination faces for best accuracy.
